title: Carnot Meets Quantum Information: Thermal Machine Driven by Probabilistic Non-orthogonal State Discrimination
authors: Tan-Ji Zhou, Yun-Qian Lin, Yu-Han Ma, C. P. Sun
abstract: While the impossibility of perfectly identifying non-orthogonal states is a cornerstone of quantum information science, their probabilistic discrimination is nonetheless permissible. Here, we propose a two-reservoir quantum machine driven by this mechanism to map its functional boundaries across the parameter space of the state overlap $μ$ and the Carnot efficiency $η_C$. Within this $η_C$-$μ$ plane, the machine exhibits phase-transition-like functional switching among a pure heat-engine phase, a mixed phase, and a dissipative phase. We identify critical thresholds governing these transitions: strong thermal driving ($η_C \ge 0.5$) unconditionally guarantees positive work extraction, whereas weak driving ($η_C \lesssim 0.13$) induces an anomalous reentrant transition, where increasing $μ$ unexpectedly restores engine functionality after a purely dissipative regime. Our results explicitly demonstrate how quantum mechanics and thermodynamics jointly constrain information-to-energy conversion.
summary: This work analyzes a theoretical thermal machine powered by the probabilistic discrimination of non-orthogonal quantum states. It maps out the operational boundaries in the parameter space defined by the Carnot efficiency and state overlap, revealing distinct phase transitions. The findings establish how quantum information constraints fundamentally limit the maximum extractable work from heat gradients.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental limits on energy conversion when a thermal machine utilizes probabilistic discrimination of non-orthogonal quantum states.
main_result: The system exhibits phase-transition-like switching in its performance region within the Carnot efficiency ($\eta_C$) and state overlap ($\mu$) plane, revealing anomalous reentrant transitions under weak driving.
method: The analysis uses a six-step thermodynamic cycle model to derive efficiencies by jointly considering quantum information bounds (Holevo-Helstrom) and classical thermodynamics constraints.
model_or_system: A two-reservoir quantum machine modeled using an ideal gas with internal quantum degrees of freedom, operating between hot ($T_h$) and cold ($T_c$) reservoirs.
key_observables: Efficiency ($\eta$), Net Work ($W_{net}$), State Overlap ($\mu$), Discrimination Accuracy ($\delta$).
important_parameters: Carnot Efficiency ($\eta_C = 1 - T_c/T_h$); critical thresholds like $\eta_C \ge 0.5$ and $\eta_C \lesssim 0.13$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes reversible operation for the joint measurement-resetting process.
figures_summary: Figure 1(b) plots the required operational region for discrimination accuracy ($\delta$) between the thermodynamic lower bound ($\delta_{lhc}$) and the quantum indistinguishability limit ($\delta_{QI}$). Figure 3 maps a phase diagram showing three distinct operating phases in the $(\eta_C, \mu)$ space.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model, derives efficiency formulas incorporating entropy terms, determines the operational constraints by comparing quantum and thermodynamic bounds, and finally maps out the resulting phase diagram to characterize functional switching.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous framework connecting non-equilibrium thermodynamics (heat engines) directly with fundamental principles of quantum information theory (state distinguishability), which is highly relevant for understanding energy extraction in quantum devices.
